questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fragile
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4 (Delicate)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 
• The word **"Fragile"** means something that is easily broken, damaged, or destroyed; it is often associated with objects or even emotional states that require careful handling. (नाज़ुक, भंगुर)

 

 
• **Example: **The antique vase is very fragile, so handle it with care.

 

 

 
• **"Delicate" **refers to something that is fine in texture, quality, or structure and is easily broken or damaged, making it a perfect synonym for "fragile." (कोमल, नाज़ुक)

 

 
• **Example: **The delicate lace on her dress looked exquisite.

 

 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate synonym of **'Fragile' **is **'Delicate'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 (Delicate)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Sturdy **(मज़बूत): Something that is strong, durable, and not easily broken or damaged.

 

 
• **Example:** The sturdy wooden table can withstand heavy loads.

 

 

 
• **Curious **(जिज्ञासु): Eager to know or learn something; inquisitive.

 

 
• **Example: **The curious child kept asking questions about the stars and planets.

 

 

 
• **Insipid** (नीरस): Lacking flavor, interest, or excitement.

 

 
• **Example:** The soup was insipid and needed more seasoning.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive voice form of the following sentence given in active voice.

Asha mailed the invitation cards yesterday.

options.text: The invitation cards were mailed by Asha yesterday.
Asha has mailed the invitation cards yesterday.
The invitation cards were being mailed by Asha yesterday.
The invitation cards have been mailed yesterday by Asha.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Asha mailed the invitation cards yesterday."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the invitation cards" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "mailed" to "were mailed" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Asha."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "yesterday" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The invitation cards were mailed by Asha yesterday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Asha has mailed the invitation cards yesterday." – Incorrect as the tense "has mailed" (present perfect) does not match the time marker "yesterday" (past event).
 
• **Option 3: **"The invitation cards were being mailed by Asha yesterday." – Incorrect as "were being mailed" implies an ongoing action, which is not the case in the given sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"The invitation cards have been mailed yesterday by Asha." – Incorrect as "have been mailed" (present perfect) is incompatible with "yesterday" (past event).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Raghav said that he had broken the cup.

options.text: Raghav said, "I had been breaking the cup."
Raghav said, "I will break the cup."
Raghav said, "I will be breaking the cup."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Raghav said that he had broken the cup.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Past perfect tense "had broken" becomes simple past "broke."**
 
 
• Past perfect in indirect speech is converted to simple past for direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb remains the same:**
 
 
• Indirect: "Raghav said"
 
• Direct: "Raghav said"
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period "."
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I broke the cup," Raghav said.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I had been breaking the cup," Raghav said.

 
 
• Incorrect tense: "had been breaking" implies an ongoing action in the past, which does not match the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "I will break the cup," Raghav said.
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "will break" implies a future action, which contradicts the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I will be breaking the cup," Raghav said.
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "will be breaking" implies a future ongoing action, which is not consistent with the original meaning.

• An **ancestor** refers to someone from whom a person is descended, typically a person from an earlier generation. It signifies someone who existed before.

• **Heir:** Refers to someone legally entitled to inherit property or titles after another's death.
 
• **Successor:** Refers to someone who follows another in a position, role, or office.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb.

All that glitters is not gold.

options.text: Gold can be the best choice.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "Appearances can be deceptive".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The proverb **"All that glitters is not gold"** means that not everything that looks attractive or valuable on the surface is actually valuable or genuine. (जो चमकता है वह सोना नहीं होता)
 
 
• **Example:** The job offer seemed perfect, but as they say, all that glitters is not gold. It turned out to be a scam.
 
 
• **"Appearances can be deceptive"** aligns with the meaning of the proverb, emphasizing that outward appearances might not reflect the true nature of something. (दिखावे धोखा दे सकते हैं)
 
 
• **Example:** That antique vase seemed valuable, but appearances can be deceptive; it was a cheap replica.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Shiny objects can be valuable** (चमकीली वस्तुएँ मूल्यवान हो सकती हैं): This suggests that anything shiny is valuable, which is not always true.
 
 
• **Example:** Not all shiny stones are diamonds; some are just glittery glass pieces.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Expensive things can be trusted** (महंगी चीज़ों पर भरोसा किया जा सकता है): This implies that higher cost equals higher quality, which is a misconception.
 
 
• **Example:** The expensive watch turned out to be fake; not everything costly is trustworthy.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Gold can be the best choice** (सोना सबसे अच्छा विकल्प हो सकता है): This focuses only on gold as a valuable asset, which is unrelated to the proverb.
 
 
• **Example:** Investing in gold is wise, but this doesn't align with the message of the proverb.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The childrens / are playing / in the / park happily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3: **'The childrens'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"childrens"** is incorrect because the plural form of "child" is "children," which is already plural and does not require an additional "s."
 
• The correct form is **"The children"**.
 
• The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: *The children are playing in the park happily.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common grammatical error:**

 
 
• **Plural forms:** Always check if a word is already plural before adding an "s" or modifying it further.
 
• **Example of incorrect usage:** "Childrens toys" (incorrect).
 
• **Correct usage:** "Children's toys" (correct).
 
 
 
• **Understanding plural nouns:**
 
 
• Some nouns have irregular plural forms, like "child" → "children" and "person" → "people."
 
• Others follow the regular rule of adding "s" or "es," like "dog" → "dogs" and "box" → "boxes."
